projects.title: Coffee rater
projects.description:
March 7, 2026

I swear I had a note about this app but I can't find it anywhere. It's completely gone. Not even in my bin.

So it's a spanish-language app because it's mainly for me and my wife, but I do want to test it with a few other people now.

It lets users write down information about the coffee beans they try and then it guides them to create a flavour profile of the coffee. Personally, i found it very interesting because i learned a lot about coffee by doing this. Especially about the difference between arabica and robusta coffee.

So today, I'm making a change that should make it easier for my wife to use the app. I'm enabling copies from the community page. So once I've rated an app, she can copy the entry and create her own flavour profile.

Next, I also want to add side-by-side comparisons.

projects.title: Content planner
projects.description:
March 5, 2026

Thought it's about time to create my own social media engine :) Of course, we're doing great work over at Willow, but we're not at a level (yet?) were I can just use my Obsidian notes as the foundation for my content strategy.

So today we're building a clean interface and self-learning content system that has a weekly rotation of 5 topics:
• product marketing
• lesson from last week
• ux law 
• cool story combined with marketing lesson
• random marketing topic

Some things that I find important:
• apparently it's better to ask for a social media post instead of a linkedin post
• every day/category will have a different skill.
• i will always have the change to edit and review. Approved drafts are saved to improve future output. 

Once approved, my LinkedIn image skill will create a visual for it. 
First impression is great, but it still needs some work on the writing style. Hashtags, really Claude? I'll have to fine-tune that a bit, and then...

Let's see how this does for a week :) 

## next time
• work with most recent note for weekly progress 
• work with most recently updated for vibing
• dates don't match the right day. 

---

March 7, 2026

I let Claude write skills for every category of post, then I edited them manually. Unfortunately, the planner can't work directly with the skills, but the prompts were integrated into the existing tool. Since it will take into account the last five approved drafts for writing a new one, the system should still be kind of self-learning, only the prompt itself won't be updated automatically (if needed)

Later, I can set up an "update skills with examples workflow" to see if that does have a significant impact on the quality. But let's test the quality first.

projects.title: Investment tracker
projects.description:
March 2, 2026

For over 10 years, i've been tracking my investments in a Numbers file. Over time, i've wanted to add more calculations and "features" but the more I add, the more I start to doubt the accuracy. So it was about time to code something.

The plan was defined rather quickly based on an csv of my existing file. 

---

March 3, 2026

Somehow the hardest app of all - just cant handle the existing data. two hours of debugging have only made things worse. Should I put the money I've spent on Claude down as an investment? It feels more like a waste at the moment...

Back to scratch is the only way i can see this working out. Trying a "soft" reset didn't lreally do it. Telling Claude to clean the existing databases didn't really work because he ran into another conflict half an hour later. 

So I told Claude to make an assessment and really start over. Judging from his reply, he agrees: "will be much faster than continuing to debug mysterious database issues".

---

March 4, 2026

Sometimes you really need to treat Claude like an intern. I've been rebuilding the app and database (I mean, Claude has been rebuilding it). But he used the same corrupted data. The whole idea behind the rebuild was to use the proper data and remove any duplicates or sources that could lead to confusion. 

After pointing this out, it seems to work. Now I'll just focus on getting everything right for me. .

Only thing left today, is adding some more graphs. 

Next month, I'll fix the data entry and dashboard views for the kids. Once this has happened, i will no longer need to import new data, so all parsing an data import scripts could be removed

I'll also add more detailed data about yields: where they come from (interest, shares, other) and about individual investments.

projects.title: Planner and goal-tracker
projects.description:
February 20, 2026

I built a personal goals tracking system that manages my career progression from daily activities up to my 15-year vision. The system lets me log daily work, set weekly goals, track quarterly objectives, and maintain long-term visions for 2030, 2035, and 2040. Every Friday when I log my activities, it automatically generates a weekly overview markdown file and saves it to my Obsidian vault in the "Weekly B2B notes" folder.

I also integrated Claude AI so I can chat about my goals and progress. I can ask questions like "When did I last work on coffee-rater?" or "What activities aren't aligned with my long-term vision?" and Claude analyzes my last 30 days of activities and all my goals to give me contextual answers. The chat remembers our conversation and helps me stay aligned with my 2030/2035/2040 vision milestones.

---

March 5, 2026

AI chat button wasn't working. I had to update some packages to make it work again.

The fact that this chat works with my memories/notes from the past weeks and aligns them with future goals and can guide me on what is useful and what is not, is insane.

projects.title: English learning app
projects.description:
February 16, 2026

I wanted to take a break from vibe coding tonight, but my wife just completed an online course and she mentioned that her next goal is to improve her English skills. Since she's already tried all sorts of tools, I have no other choice but to vibe-code something.

I've got a pretty interesting idea that should work perfectly in the AI era. But before I start, I'm going to use Mistral's Le Chat to fine-tune my prompt. That's something I've not done enough for previous projects.

Asked it to be motivational and flower-themed. Super impressed with the suggested prompt. i'm afraid the scope will be a bit out of my comfort zone, but all the apps have been and I should always aim a step higher.

---

February 17, 2026

Yesterday I wrapped up the plan. Today, I executed the plan. (Hit enter and let Claude do it's thing)

---

February 26, 2026

Committing and pushing to github today. Then I'll deploy it via Railway. Super curious as to what i'll see and how many bugs will need to be fixed...

Biggest issue is connecting the database. I thought it would be straightforward since we've done it before, but it is't. I should have taken better notes from the previous project. I asked Claude how we did it for the coffee rater app and hope to make progress with this but it sounds more complicated than I remembered. But I'm also getting so security warnings from deprecated packages. And even though Claude tells me not to worry, I want to get this fixed first.

Think I'm understanding the issue now. At some point, I created a duplicate of the coffee rater app, but Claude has based this new app on the outdated, incomplete first version. Another few hours of learning money paid.

I suddenly noticed when Drizzle ORM was outdated. In the end, the solution wasn't that difficult but I thought I was fixing a new unexpected problem instead of the same one as before.

Haha, it's still not working to create an account. Wouldn't be too much fun if everything worked right. Even though a lot changed in the background, I'm still seeing the same error when trying to create an account.

Still had a problem with Vite which Claude found because I reminded him again to compare with the successful coffee tracker app. Now i can log in but of course we have some front end issues now. The learning levels exist but aren't being shown. Well, first they weren't in the database but that was fixed rather quickly even though I have no clue how.

---

February 27, 2026

Couldn't make it work yesterday and couldn't sleep this morning. So back at it before the kids wake up. Found another localhost link so hopefully removing that will fix it now. Or it will reveal another issue. 

While waiting for the app to rebuild and redeploy over 20 times, I explored Railway and found the "observability" tab. Very clean dashboards but can't really make sense of what they mean. Will need to look into egress later because the numbers of predicted usage and actual usage don't match at all. We're talking cents but I wanna avoid adding another paid subscription for now.

Aha. Another issue we had with the coffee rater app. Session cookies aren't being created. It's funny how 2 lines of code can break an entire app.

---

March 3, 2026

I've completed the first three levels without issues but that seems to be the end of it. For an app that should learn and create new levels, it's a bit disappointing. 

I've no instructed the tool to create two additional levels every time the current levels are completed. One level should focus on improving what needs reinforcements and the other level should offer something new. It will use Claude API in the background to create these levels. Surprisingly, there were no bugs and it seems to be working. I see 3 new levels in my account.

But I'll have it create 3 new levels at a time instead. One isn't a lot, so the reinforcement level will be quite empty or get very repetitive as is.

I also made some changes to the app's logic. Now every level needed a 100% success rate to succeed but I've changed that to 80%.

Did have a few minor issues such as "it is one o'clock" being transcribed as "it is 1:00" - and spelling exercises were showing the English word. Both were easy fixes fortunately. Don't know if the model suddenly got better or if the foundation is actually this solid lol.

projects.title: Company finance tracking
projects.description:
February 9, 2026

I just realised that I don't have a solid view of my business expenses. I know that I typically earn more than I spend, but how much?
No better way to find out, than to vibe code a desktop app to keep track of invoices sent and received. 
Initially, it doesn't need to be complicated. The only tricky part is the difference between one-off expenses, and monthly, quarterly and yearly recurring ones. 

When this part works, I also want to develop a personal tracker. I've been tracking my investments in a Number sheet for over 10 years and it's getting kind of clunky. I'm also pretty sure there are some mistakes in my logic. So I can fix it and add it to my tracker.

Later on, if everything works, I could look at automating parts. I'm especially thinking about syncing expenses. Open banking is something I'm not going to get involved with, though.

This session, Claude generated:
• 26 Swift files (~3,700 lines of code)
• 24 source files
• 2 test files (30+ unit tests)
• 6 documentation files (comprehensive guides)
• 100% of planned features implemented

This version included an App with CloudKit. It sounded like an overkill for an app that just needs to sync between my devices, but what do I know? Only after trying to set it up in Xcode, my suspicions were confirmed.

It cost less than $5 so far. But it will probably end up costing a lot more as I need quite some back and forth to roll back Cloud capabilities that aren't available to free plans. Easily spent an extra hour on this as well. 

Damn, it looks like a real Apple App. Not what I expected but pretty nice apart from some alignment issues.

---

February 10, 2026

After some further back and forth, I got the app to work with decent padding too.

Now, I'm most definitely not going to use the same app for personal finances because it's going to break again. But I can use the structure and learnings from this to create another one.

Only thing left to do now is figure out how i can add this app to my desktop and how to give it a logo so I don't have to run it from Xcode every time.

---

March 2, 2026

Time to implement the next changes:
• net profit = difference between income and expenses without VAT
• (later include more detailed calculations for VAT based on category)
• Save names of expenses (eg charging) + detailed overview of expenses per name instead of category
• quarterly and yearly costs -> split over months but only if the expense is more than 250 euros.

 It worked pretty well but I had to delete the database and start from scratch since there was no database backup. Ah well, I didn't have that much in there yet anyway.

projects.title: Rent scraper
projects.description:
February 5, 2026

We're looking for larger place to live but there aren't many larger houses for rent.
It's getting quite tiring to check 10+ real estate pages from time to time, so would be great if I could make a scraper that pulls in new houses for rent that match my requirements.

Just planning with Claude Code cost a surprising lot of tokens. It took around 250k tokens just to analyse previous projects and find parts to re-use. I wonder if that was worth the effort. At least, it did come up with a very detailed and well-structured plan.

While fine-tuning the plan it helped to stop and clarify that I'm looking for a simple solution. That made Claude suggest to create an email digest instead of an app.

First result looks pretty nice - however the scrapers don't work well. Only 13 listings were found from the first three implemented websites. 2 passed the filters but they didn't actually meet the requirements that we set at the start.

To get all the listings, Claude had to create scrapers for every page. It took two tries for most websites but five out of fourteen didn't work according to Claude. I asked what I could do manually, but the suggestions were and API or installing more complicated dependencies. Instead, I inspected a page and copied the exact path to where the room numbers is on the page. This helped me fix one scraper. On to the next now.

Made some small changes to how projects and days are being parsed.
One project per note file: Each Obsidian note is now treated as a single project, regardless of how many date sections (H2 headers) it contains. 
Chronological ordering: Date sections within a note are now sorted chronologically (oldest to newest) before being processed and aggregated.
Aggregated content: All work sessions from different dates are combined into a single project entry with:
• The earliest date as the main project date
• All content from all sessions aggregated
• All learnings combined
• Maximum intensity across all sessions
• A new workDates array that tracks all the dates you worked on that project
Clean titles: Project titles no longer have "(Day 1)", "(Day 2)" labels.

---

February 5, 2026

The changes from yesterday didn't really work out the way I wanted.
I trusted Claude to just change everything at once but it didn't work.
I then tried again, giving more and clearer instructions but it almost reversed the changes instead.
Today, I tried implementing the small changes one by one, instead.
The key learning here is that you can't ask too much at once. I actually knew this from the very first time I started vibe coding but i was starting to trust the machine too much.

projects.title: Sally, customer success oracle
projects.description:
January 28, 2026

Just made a Slack bot that everyone in the team can talk to to ask questions about our successful customers. 

But it can also answer other questions like: 
• Which customers are in IT? 
• Which customers have an office manager? 
• Who had the most impressions last year? 

How does it work? 

Two simple n8n workflows. 
Every time a new success story gets added (or updated) to Webflow, it gets synced to a database 
Slack messages get passed on to an AI Agent who only takes the database as a single source of truth. The reply gets sent back to the same slack channel.

---

January 29, 2026

Sally lives on ww.willow.co/success-stories too now.
Been wanting to implement this for months but never felt confident about how to do it.
Since I got more experience with webhooks now, I gave it another shot and it was easier than expected.
Starting with a script for Webflow written by ChatGPT, it was easy enough to connect it to n8n and send back replies to the web page. 
Styling it was something I could easily do manually as well.
Pretty happy with the result.

projects.title: Wardrobe
projects.description:
January 16, 2026

First time working with Claude Code. Developed fully locally.
Learning here is that the main file is definitely too large. 
Wondering why CSS isn't separated for example.
Also the stack was too light to make it work visually, but again maybe it's related to the CSS too.
Good but expensive learning experience (around 28$)

---

January 27, 2026
Converted desktop app to web app - Transformed the CustomTkinter desktop wardrobe manager into a Flask-based web application
Unified database - Merged separate wardrobe.db and wardrobe_fer.db into single database with `wardrobe` field to distinguish owners
Added search & filter - Implemented debounced search (300ms), type filtering, and sorting by rating/brand/date
Built REST API - Created 10+ Flask endpoints for CRUD operations, search, filter, sort, and undo functionality
Vanilla JS frontend - Developed SPA with state management, API client, and modular components (ItemCard, ItemModal, SearchFilter)
CSS theme system - Implemented CSS variables for instant theme switching between Kjell's earthy and Fer's pink color schemes
Preserved features - Maintained all original functionality: color-coded cards, 10-star ratings, color picker, edit/delete with undo
Migrated 72 items - Successfully transferred all items from Kjell's wardrobe with full data integrity and backups
Responsive design - Built mobile-friendly grid layout with auto-fill columns and media queries for various screen sizes
Complete documentation - Created README, INSTALL, QUICKSTART guides plus verification scripts for easy setup and troubleshooting

Key Features
• View items organized by clothing type
• Add/edit/delete items with confirmation
• Color-coded item cards with contrast text
• 10-star rating system
• Color picker for custom colors
• Switch between Kjell's and Fer's wardrobes
• Undo delete (10-second window)
• Automatic data persistence
• Search - Full-text search across brand, model, materials with debouncing
• Filter - Dropdown to filter by specific clothing type
• Sort - Multiple sort options (rating desc, brand asc, date desc)
• Responsive - Mobile-friendly grid layout
• Keyboard shortcuts - ESC to close modals
• Real-time updates - Observer pattern for reactive UI
• API access - RESTful endpoints for external integration

---

March 5, 2026

Some time ago, I added a shortcut so I can launch the app by typing "wardrobe" in terminal. That's pretty easy. Made some tiny changes today:
• Renamed categories that were still in Dutch
• Reorganised by tops and bottoms instead of alphabetically.
• Made categories collapsable.

Claude took care of it while I took a break. What a life.
